articles.title: Have You Ever Met a Lion?
articles.dek: A zoo keeper tells funny and scary stories from work.
paras: For our school magazine, Mia Chen, 14, talked to Sam Brooks. Sam is a zoo keeper at our city zoo. He has worked there for ten years. He looks after lions, monkeys and penguins. Here is their interview.

Mia: Have you ever been afraid of an animal? Sam: Yes, I have. I have worked with lions and monkeys, but I have never touched a big snake. I just look at snakes from a safe place. My friend Tara is the snake keeper. She has never been afraid of them!

Mia: Have you ever had a bad day at work? Sam: Of course. Last summer, a monkey took my hat and ran away. I have never run so fast! Everyone laughed, but I wasn't happy. I got my hat back an hour later. It was wet and dirty.
Mia: Have you ever slept at the zoo? Sam: Yes, I have. Once a baby tiger was ill, so I stayed all night. I have never been so tired! But the tiger got better, and that made me very happy.

Mia: Have you ever been on TV? Sam: No, I haven't. But I have met some famous people at the zoo. Last year, a singer visited us. She loves animals, but she has never touched a penguin. So I let her give our penguins their fish.

Mia: Has anyone in your family ever worked with animals? Sam: My sister has. She is a vet. We have never worked in the same place, but we often talk about our animals. She has often helped me with a sick animal.

Mia: Would you like to give some advice to students? Sam: Yes! It is a hard job, but I have never wanted a different one. You must love animals, and you must not mind the smell! Have you ever thought about this job? Then visit the zoo and ask questions.

articles.title: Our Day at the Castle
articles.dek: Follow Nina on a school trip, hour by hour.
paras: Hello, everybody! This is Nina's travel blog. Today my class is visiting an old castle by the sea. I have just arrived, and I am so excited! The castle is very big. It is about seven hundred years old.

10:30 – We have already seen the front gate and the big yard. Inside, the rooms are cold and dark. There are old swords on the walls. The guide is called Mr Hill. He has just told us a funny story about a ghost. I haven't seen the ghost yet, but my friend Sam says he is scared.

11:45 – We have already climbed the tower. There are 120 steps, and I have already counted them twice! My legs are tired, but the view is great. I have just taken a photo of the sea. I can see small boats and many birds.

1:00 – It is lunchtime. I haven't eaten yet, and I'm very hungry. Sam has already finished his sandwich. He eats so fast! We have just found a nice place in the garden. We are sitting under a big tree.

2:30 – The shop is next. I haven't bought anything yet. Have you ever bought a postcard from a castle? I want one for my grandma. My teacher has just said that we have only twenty minutes, so I must hurry.

4:00 – We are on the bus now. Have you read my blog yet? I have already written a lot, but I haven't shown you my photos yet. I will put them online tonight. I haven't seen the ghost, but it was a great day. Bye for now!

articles.title: The Story of Jeans
articles.dek: Your jeans are older than you think.

sources.name: Levi Strauss & Co.: The History of Denim
HISTORY: Levi Strauss and Jacob Davis patent blue jeans

paras: Look at your clothes. Are you wearing jeans? Many people are. Jeans are very popular today, but they have a long story. Let's find out how it began.

Jeans began in the 1800s. A man called Jacob Davis was a tailor. A tailor makes clothes. Some of his customers were workers, and their trousers often tore. Davis had an idea. He put small metal rivets on the corners of the pockets. The trousers became much stronger.

Davis wanted a patent for his idea. A patent says that an idea is yours. But he didn't have enough money for it. So he wrote to Levi Strauss. Strauss sold cloth to Davis. He liked the idea. In 1873, the two men got the patent together.

At first, people called them waist overalls. Workers wore them because they were cheap, strong and comfortable. Around 1960, young people began to call them jeans. Soon more and more young people wore them.

Since then, jeans have changed a lot. They have become long, short, wide and thin. Designers have made them in many colours. People have also added patches and paint to their jeans. Today there are jeans for babies, for grandparents and for everyone in between.

Is the story over? No. People in almost every country wear jeans today. My uncle has had the same pair for ten years, and he hasn't thrown them away. Have you ever worn jeans for a whole week? Perhaps your jeans will have a long story too.
